"# Production Dockerfile for FastAPI Backend & Frontend (Option C: Local Hardened)
FROM python:3.12-slim

ENV PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
    PIP_NO_CACHE_DIR=1

WORKDIR /app

# Install system dependencies
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    curl \
    libpq-dev \
    gcc \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Install Python requirements
COPY backend/requirements.txt /app/backend/requirements.txt
RUN pip install --upgrade pip && pip install -r /app/backend/requirements.txt

# Copy application directories
COPY backend/ /app/backend/
COPY frontend/ /app/frontend/
COPY data/ /app/data/

EXPOSE 8000

# Health check
HEALTHCHECK --interval=10s --timeout=5s --start-period=15s --retries=3 \
  CMD curl -f http://localhost:8000/health || exit 1

# Production command without reload
CMD ["uvicorn", "app.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000", "--app-dir", "backend", "--workers", "1"]
"

"# =============================================================================
# The Lenny Growth Assistant — Environment Configuration
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Database Configuration (PostgreSQL)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Local Dev: postgresql://lenny:[REDACTED]@localhost:5432/lenny
# Production Docker Compose: postgresql://lenny:[REDACTED]@postgres:5432/lenny
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://lenny:[REDACTED]@localhost:5432/lenny
POSTGRES_PASSWORD=[REDACTED]

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. LLM Providers
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Default Provider: "gemini" or "ollama"
LLM_PROVIDER=gemini

# Google Gemini API Key (Required for Cloud provider)
GEMINI_API_KEY=[REDACTED]

# Local Ollama Configuration (Optional, for Local provider)
OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434
OLLAMA_MODEL=llama3.2:latest

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Pi Agent Service
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Local Dev: http://localhost:3001
# Production Docker Compose: http://pi-agent:3001
PI_AGENT_URL=http://localhost:3001
PI_AGENT_PORT=3001

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Security & CORS
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sanitization mode for HTML Visual Artifacts: "sanitize" or "reject"
ARTIFACT_SANITIZATION_MODE=sanitize

# Allowed CORS origins (comma-separated, e.g. "http://localhost:8000,http://127.0.0.1:8000" or "*")
ALLOWED_ORIGINS=*
"

"# Security Architecture & Safeguards — The Lenny Growth Assistant

This document outlines the defense-in-depth security model implemented in **The Lenny Growth Assistant**.

---

## 1. Untrusted Transcript & Ingestion Isolation

- **Source Code Isolation**: All transcript data is treated as untrusted text. No scripts, executable files, or build scripts from source transcript repositories are ever executed.
- **Normalization Pipeline**: Ingestion parses raw transcripts into static JSON (`episodes.json`, `chunks.json`, `topics.json`) through strict schema validators (`app/ingestion/validator.py`).
- **Prompt Injection Defense**: When transcript chunks are passed to LLMs, system prompts use explicit boundary delimiters (`<<<TRANSCRIPT_CONTEXT>>>` and `<<<USER_QUERY>>>`), instructing the model to treat transcript text exclusively as reference data and ignore any embedded instructions.

---

## 2. Dual-Layer HTML Artifact Sanitization & Sandboxing

HTML Visual Artifacts undergo two independent defensive layers before display:

### Layer 1: Backend Rust-Based `nh3` Sanitization
- Implemented in [`backend/app/security.py`](file:///c:/Users/[REDACTED_USER]/Desktop/12%20week%20thing/Lenny/backend/app/security.py) using the `nh3` library (Rust Ammonia engine).
- **Tag Allowlist**: Only safe formatting and structural tags are permitted (`div`, `span`, `p`, `table`, `h1`-`h6`, `style`, `section`, etc.).
- **Strict Tag Stripping**: All `<script>`, `<iframe>`, `<object>`, `<embed>`, `<applet>`, `<form>`, and `<meta http-equiv>` tags are stripped or rejected.
- **Attribute Allowlist**: Event handlers (`onclick`, `onerror`, `onload`, `onmouseover`, etc.) are stripped.
- **URL Scheme Validation**: Only `http`, `https`, and `mailto` URL schemes are allowed; `javascript:`, `data:`, and `vbscript:` schemes are neutralized.

### Layer 2: Client-Side Isolated Iframe Sandboxing
- Rendered in [`frontend/index.html`](file:///c:/Users/[REDACTED_USER]/Desktop/12%20week%20thing/Lenny/frontend/index.html) inside an `<iframe>` config

```
"# The Lenny Growth Assistant

A production-grade, grounded AI knowledge platform, product growth advisor, and structured content generator built on top of **221 Lenny's Podcast transcripts**. It combines PostgreSQL Full-Text Search (FTS), Pi Agent orchestration, multi-turn session persistence, specialized writing skills (Ship 30 for 30), dual LLM provider support (Google Gemini Cloud + Local Ollama), and dual-layer sandboxed HTML/Markdown artifact generation.

---

## 1. What the Project Is
The Lenny Growth Assistant is designed to make hundreds of hours of tactical advice from world-class product leaders, growth practitioners, and founders instantly accessible, verifiable, and actionable. Rather than generating ungrounded summaries, it synthesizes exact frameworks directly from verified transcript turns, providing deep links to YouTube timestamps and exporting clean publication-ready artifacts.

---

## 2. Architecture Overview
```
[ Browser Client (:8000) ]
        │
        ▼ (HTTP REST / Static Assets)
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    lenny-network                           │
│                                                            │
│  FastAPI Backend (:8000)                                   │
│  ├── Session & Memory Management                           │
│  ├── PostgreSQL Full-Text Search & Topic Boosting          │
│  ├── HTML Sanitization Engine (Rust-based nh3)             │
│  └── Static File Server (/ & /static)                      │
│         │                             │                    │
│         ▼ (Private :5432)             ▼ (Private :3001)    │
│  PostgreSQL 16                     Pi Agent Service        │
│  (GIN FTS Indexes)                 (Node/TypeScript)       │
│

Here is the complete, beginner-friendly guide for a new developer starting this project from scratch using Docker Compose:

---

## 🚀 Quickstart Guide for New Developers (Docker Compose)

### 📋 Prerequisites
Before starting, ensure you have:
1. **Docker Desktop** installed and running on your machine.
2. *(Optional for Cloud LLM)*: A **Google Gemini API Key** from [Google AI Studio](https://aistudio.google.com/).
3. *(Optional for Local LLM)*: [Ollama](https://ollama.ai/) installed and running locally with `ollama pull llama3.2`.

---

### Step 1: Navigate to the Project Root
Open your terminal (PowerShell, Command Prompt, or Terminal) in the project directory:
```bash
cd "c:\Users\shrav\Desktop\12 week thing\Lenny"
```

---

### Step 2: Set Up Your Environment File (`.env`)
Create your `.env` file by copying the template:

**Windows (PowerShell):**
```powershell
Copy-Item .env.example .env
```

**macOS / Linux:**
```bash
cp .env.example .env
```

Open `.env` in your editor and paste your **Gemini API key**:
```env
GEMINI_API_KEY=[REDACTED]
LLM_PROVIDER=gemini
```
*(If you don't have a key right now, you can still test with local Ollama or explore the interface).*

---

### Step 3: Launch Everything with One Command
Run the production compose build command:

```bash
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up --build
```
> 💡 **Tip**: If you want to run it in the background, append `-d`:
> ```bash
> docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up --build -d
> ```

---

### Step 4: Access the Application 🎉
Once the containers are healthy (you will see Uvicorn running on port 8000 in logs):

Open your browser and visit:
👉 **[http://localhost:8000](http://localhost:8000)**

---

### 🔍 What Docker Compose Sets Up Automatically

| Service | What It Does | Access / Port |
|---|---|---|
| **`postgres`** | PostgreSQL 16 database. **Auto-populates all 297 episodes & 14,933 transcript chunks** on first boot. | Private (Internal only) |
| **`pi-agent`** | Node.js / TypeScript AI Agent service handling Ship 30 writing skills and LLM orchestration. | Private (`:3001` internal) |
| **`backend`** | Python 3.12 FastAPI server running the RAG search pipeline, HTML sanitization, and serving the frontend UI. | **Public (`http://localhost:8000`)** |

---

### 🛠️ Handy Management Commands

- **View Live Logs**:
  ```bash
  docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml logs -f
  ```
- **View Backend Logs Only**:
  ```bash
  docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml logs -f backend
  ```
- **Stop the Containers**:
  ```bash
  docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml down
  ```
- **Complete Reset (Wipes Database Volume to restart fresh)**:
  ```bash
  docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml down -v
  ```

    """Background task to initialize tables and populate processed transcript dataset if empty."""

        print(f"Warning during startup database check: {e}")

    import threading
    t = threading.Thread(target=_async_db_init, daemon=True)
    t.start()"

args.Instruction: "Track app_status ('setting_up' -> 'ready') in _async_db_init and expose via /health and /status"
args.ReplacementContent:
"# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Startup Lifecycle & System Readiness (Checkpoints 4 & 5)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
_app_state: Dict[str, Any] = {
    "status": "setting_up",
    "db_ready": False,
    "episodes_count": 0,
    "chunks_count": 0,
}


def _async_db_init():
    """Background task to initialize tables and populate processed transcript dataset if empty."""
    try:
        Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)
        ep_count = 0
        chunk_count = 0
        with SessionLocal() as db:
            ep_count = db.query(Episode).count()
            chunk_count = db.query(TranscriptChunk).count()

        if ep_count == 0 and DATA_PROCESSED_DIR.exists():
            print("Database is empty. Automatically loading initial transcript dataset in background...")
            _app_state["status"] = "setting_up"
            load_processed_data_to_db(DATA_PROCESSED_DIR)
            print("Initial transcript dataset successfully loaded.")
            with SessionLocal() as db:
                ep_count = db.query(Episode).count()
                chunk_count = db.query(TranscriptChunk).count()

        _app_state["status"] = "ready"
        _app_state["db_ready"] = True
        _app_state["episodes_count"] = ep_count
        _app_state["chunks_count"] = chunk_count
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Warning during startup database check: {e}")
        _app_state["status"] = "ready"
        _app_state["db_ready"] = True


@app.on_event("startup")
def startup_db_init():
    import threading
    t = threading.Thread(target=_async_db_init, daemon=True)

### 2. What is the PostgreSQL warning and how is it fixed?
```
WARNING: database "lenny" has no actual collation version, but a version was recorded
```
- **What it is**: PostgreSQL 16 on Alpine Linux uses Alpine's `musl` standard library. Because `musl` does not provide versioned locale collations (unlike standard Debian/Ubuntu `glibc`), PostgreSQL logs this benign informational warning whenever a client connects.
- **Impact**: Completely harmless warning that has no effect on queries, full-text search, or persistence.
- **Permanent Fix**: Switching from `postgres:16-alpine` to standard `postgres:16` (Debian-based with full `glibc` locale versioning) eliminates this message.

---

```

[Gemini gemini-2.5-flash-lite Attempt Failed]: 404 Model no longer available
[Gemini gemini-flash-latest Attempt Failed]: 400 Thinking level MINIMAL is not supported
```

  - `gemini-2.5-flash`: The free-tier key reached its daily request ceiling (20 requests/day).
  - `gemini-2.5-flash-lite`: Deprecated upstream by Google in favor of `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`.
  - `gemini-flash-latest`: Failed because of an unsupported thinking parameter.

    $$\text{gemini-2.5-flash} \longrightarrow \text{gemini-3.5-flash} \longrightarrow \text{gemini-3.5-flash-lite} \longrightarrow \text{gemini-3-flash-preview} \longrightarrow \text{gemini-3.1-pro-preview}$$
